name: CF7 Visited Pages URL Tracking
author: Chetan Vaghela

sections.description:
CF7 Visited Pages URL Tracking enhances Contact Form 7 by recording the pages a visitor views before submitting a form and automatically including those URLs in the email notification.

The plugin stores the visitor’s page history in browser cookies. When a Contact Form 7 form is submitted, the list of previously visited pages is inserted into the email body using a simple mail tag. This helps website owners better understand visitor behavior, identify user interests, and gain additional context for enquiries.

Whether you’re collecting sales leads, support requests, or general enquiries, knowing which pages a visitor viewed before contacting you can provide valuable insights.

Features

  • Track the pages visitors view before submitting a Contact Form 7 form.
  • Automatically include visited page URLs in email notifications.
  • Simple mail tag integration with Contact Form 7.
  • Helps understand visitor navigation and user intent.
  • Lightweight and easy to configure.
  • Compatible with the latest versions of Contact Form 7.

Use Cases

  • Understand the visitor’s journey before making an enquiry.
  • Improve lead qualification by identifying pages of interest.
  • Provide additional context for support requests.
  • Analyze visitor behavior without using complex analytics tools.
  • Help sales teams understand what content influenced a submission.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install it through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Open CF7 – Track Visited Pages from the WordPress admin menu.

  4. Add the following mail tag to your Contact Form 7 email template:

    [CF7VPUT_VISITED_Details]

  5. Save your Contact Form 7 settings and start tracking visitor page history.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin require Contact Form 7?

Yes. This plugin extends the functionality of Contact Form 7 and requires it to be installed and activated.

How do I display the visited pages in the email?

Simply add the following mail tag to your Contact Form 7 email template:

[CF7VPUT_VISITED_Details]

What information is tracked?

The plugin records the URLs of pages visited before the form submission and includes them in the notification email.

Does the plugin require any additional configuration?

No. After activation, simply add the mail tag to your Contact Form 7 email template.
